anti_patterns: hand-written tokenizer and parser with explicit token-list threading instead of DCG notation
cuts and if-then-else used for dispatch where first-argument clause indexing would do
binop/4 has a catch-all clause after the specific ones, so it leaves choicepoints and can add an invalid_op solution on backtracking
evaluate/3 leaves choicepoints because of the nondeterministic combine/binop clauses
member/2 inside an if-then-else condition to scan for a non-ok status
explicit recursion in eval_all/3 instead of maplist
memberchk/2 on operator atoms for dispatch instead of separate clauses
justification: The recursive-descent parser follows the grammar closely and threads token lists as difference-list-like pairs. It does not use DCG notation, which is the idiomatic Prolog tool for this task, and it relies on cuts and if-then-else more than necessary. The evaluator uses head pattern matching for AST nodes and short-circuits statuses reasonably. However, the catch-all `binop(_, _, _, invalid_op)` clause is reachable on backtracking, `eval_all` reimplements `maplist`, and the `member`-based status check is clumsy. Decomposition into tokenizer, parser, and evaluator is clear and readable, but the design is somewhat repetitive (expr_rest and term_rest are near duplicates)..
